title.en: Practical 7: Detection of adulterants in food samples

text.en: How can a pinch of food and a glass of water expose a cheat?

The aim is to detect adulterants in food samples such as pepper, honey, sugar, chilli powder, green peas and tea powder. The materials are beakers, a glass bowl, a spoon and a matchbox.
Take beakers of water labelled A to E, add the given samples and observe what happens in each beaker, such as floating, sinking, colour change or dissolving.
Record your observations and the indication of adulteration in the table. Adulteration means mixing a cheaper or harmful substance in food, so such tests help us choose safe food.
